messages:
arjun: Heads up — seeing repeated node provisioning in europe-west1 on the ml-inference GPU pool since ~08:45 UTC. HPA spikes from queue-length metric then CA spins up nodes, pods schedule, HPA immediately scales down -> nodes sit idle and we pay preemptible churn. Anyone else seeing this?
zoe: yep noticed too, cost alert fired. looks like queue_length metric is noisy for short bursts. :frowning:
maria: also saw a couple slow image pulls yesterday — GCP egress quotas were around 90% on that project. could be slowing node startup so the HPA oscillation window is misaligned with CA provisioning time.
arjun: exact problem. HPA reacts in <1m to queue spikes, CA takes ~2-4m to provision GPUs in that region under load -> by the time nodes come up, HPA has already scaled down replicas. CA then marks nodes unneeded, scale-down waits and we pay for minutes of idle GPUs.
zoe: ugh. Should we add a stabilization window on the HPA and/or a small "warm" GPU pool?
maria: propose two-pronged: 1) HPA behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds = 300 (5m) + scaleUpWindow maybe 30s; 2) a tiny warm nodepool (1-2 A10s) in europe-west1 with taint "warm=true:NoSchedule" and nodeSelector/affinity for inference-critical pods so scheduling is fast.
arjun: agree. Also tweak CA settings: increase --max-node-provision-time to 6m and set expander to least-waste. That should reduce thrash.
kai: quick note — VPA is recommending lower CPU for some workers; if pods get smaller resources they might be scheduled onto different node types and change bin-packing, could make provisioning slower. We should pin resource requests for the HPA target pods for now.
infra-bot: Incident detected: repeated GPU provisioning events in europe-west1 at 2024-07-22T08:45Z -> metric: cluster.autoscaler.provision_attempts >= 6 in 10m window. Page -> #oncall (sre-oncall).
sre-oncall: I'll look at CA logs and confirm provision times. Could you paste the HPA YAML and metric config?
arjun: snippet of the HPA we're using:
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-queue-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference-worker
  minReplicas: 0
  maxReplicas: 12
  metrics:
    - type: External
      external:
        metric:
          name: queue_length
        target:
          type: AverageValue
          averageValue: "5"
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
```
zoe: current scaleDown is only 60s which is the root cause. if CA needs ~3m, HPA should wait longer.
maria: action plan: 1) increase scaleDown to 300s on HPA (arjun) 2) create warm pool 1-2 A10s with taint "warm=true:NoSchedule" and nodeSelector/affinity for critical pods (kai) 3) CA tuning: --max-node-provision-time=360s + expander=least-waste (sre-oncall) 4) temporary: pin requests on inference-worker to avoid VPA surprises (maria)
arjun: I'll open the HPA PR now. assigning to kai for warm pool make + test.
kai: grabbing it. I'll set up a canary warm pool in europe-west1 and run a synthetic burst to validate. will report back with cost delta. :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: I'll check CA events and cloud quotas (egress). if egress quota is the blocker we might pre-pull images to the node image cache on the warm pool.
maria: one more thought — switch HPA metric to a slightly smoothed metric: queue_length_avg_30s or use a moving average exporter. That will reduce transient spikes.
arjun: good idea. for now we do the 5m stabilization + warm pool and smoothing next sprint.
zoe: thanks team. can we add an alert for CA provision time > 180s? tha'tll catch regressions.
infra-bot: Task created: #infra-452 add HPA stabilization + warm pool canary. assignees: arjun, kai, sre-oncall.
arjun: added PR link (WIP): https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/3123 — updating now.
kai: running canary, will post results ~09:30 UTC. :coffee:
